body_ar:
الجمع بين الحديث: إن الله لا يقبض العلم انتزاعا، والقول إن القرآن يمحى من المصاحف والصدور في ليلة من الليالي كيف يمكن الجمع بين الحديث: إن الله لا يقبض العلم انتزاعا، والقول إن القرآن يمحى من المصاحف والصدور في ليلة من الليالي؟

هذا إنما يكون في آخر الزمان عندما يرفع العلم ويكثر الجهل ويبقى القرآن للتبرك فقط ولا يبقى للعلم، فإن القرآن من رفعه أن يبقى للتبرك فقط فيبقى رقى تعلق على المجانين والمصابين أو زخارف تزين بها البيوت ويهجر العمل به والحكم به في النهار ويهجر القيام به في الليل، فهذا من رفعه وقد شاهدتم بعض ذلك.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الختمة للميت

هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟ إن وصول ثواب القرءان للميت بعد موته محل خلاف بين أهل العلم فمذهب مالك والشافعي أنه لا يصل وذلك أن الأصل قول الله تعالى ﴿أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى﴾ فعلى هذا الأصل لا يصل هذا العمل بعد الموت أما أبو حنيفة وأحمد فذهبا إلى وصوله قياسا لقراءة القرءان على الصدقة و الحج و العمرة وغير ذلك من أنواع القرب وقد اتفق على أن الصدقة و الدعاء يصلان قطعا وما عداهما كله داخل في الخلاف لأن الصدقة والدعاء ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة عن النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم وكذلك الحج و العمرة ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة أما ما سوى ذلك كله فلم يرد فيه نص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويبقي الخلاف هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس أو ليس من المقدرات فيمكن القياس فيه هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه و على هذا فالذين يفعلون الختمة عن دبر الميت ويريدون إيصالها إليه فالأحوط بهم والأفضل لهم أن يتصدقوا عنه و أن يدعوا له فهذا الذي يصل بلا خلاف.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الخسف الذي سيقع في الشرق والغرب وجزيرة العرب

ما هو الخسف الذي سيقع في الشرق والغرب وجزيرة العرب؟

الخسف هو الزلزال الذي يقتضي أن يدخل وجه الأرض تحت بعض طبقاتها وهذا من أشد أنواع الزلازل، ووقع كثير من الخسوف في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها، ولكن لا يمكن الجزم بأن خسفا من هذه الخسوف هو المقصود في الحديث، وإن كانت ثلاثة خسوف قد جاءت متقاربة أحدها بالمشرق والآخر بالمغرب والآخر بجزيرة العرب، فالذي حصل في المشرق هو الخسف الذي سمعتم به في إيران والخسف الذي حصل بالمغرب هو خسف مدينة الأصنام بالجزائر، والخسف الذي بجزيرة العرب هو خسف مدينة الذمار باليمن، ولكن لا يمكن الجزم بأنها هي المقصودة في الحديث بل هذه آيات كلها ومواعظ، والله تعالى يقول: {وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِالْآَيَاتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا (59)} [الإسراء] وهي تذكير للعباد بالإيمان بالله سبحانه وتعالى وحده، ولكن لا يجزم بأنها هي المقصودة بالحديث لأنه لم يرد ما يدل على خصوص ذلك.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الذكر عند شيخ مخصوص

اشتراط أخذ الذكر عن شيخ واحد مخصوص؟ أن الذكر مثل غيره من أمور الدين يؤخذ عن كل من رواه و كل من نقله والآن يؤخذ من الكتب أيضا فإذا رجع الإنسان إلى صحيح البخاري أو صحيح مسلم أو الموطأ أو إلى كتب الأذكار فأخذ منها هذه الأذكار فذلك كاف فليس هو ذا خصوصية زائدة على ما في الأحكام كلها.
body_en:
Reconciling the hadith 'God does not take knowledge away by snatching it out' with the statement that the Qur'an will be erased from the written copies and from people's breasts on one of the nights. How can one reconcile the hadith 'God does not take knowledge away by snatching it out' with the statement that the Qur'an will be erased from the written copies and from people's breasts on one of the nights?

This will only be at the end of time, when knowledge is taken up and ignorance becomes widespread, and the Qur'an remains only as a thing to seek blessing by and no longer remains for knowledge. For part of the Qur'an's being taken up is that it should remain only as a thing to seek blessing by — so that it remains as charms hung on the insane and the afflicted, or as ornaments with which houses are decorated, while acting by it and judging by it in the daytime is abandoned, and standing in prayer with it at night is abandoned. This is part of its being taken up; and you have witnessed some of that.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The khatmah for the deceased

Is the khatmah for the deceased permissible or not — the one that is called al-salkah?

Whether the reward of [reciting] the Qur'an reaches the deceased after his death is a point on which the scholars differ. The position (madhhab) of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that it does not reach him, on the ground that the governing principle is the words of God, exalted is He: {Or has he not been told of what is in the scrolls of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled [what he was charged with] — that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that a person shall have nothing but what he has striven for, and that his striving shall be seen, and then he shall be repaid for it with the fullest repayment} (Sūrat al-Najm 53:36–41). On this principle, this act does not reach him after death. As for Abu Hanifah and Ahmad, they held that it does reach him, by analogical reasoning (qiyās) from the recitation of the Qur'an to voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), to hajj, to the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah), and to the other kinds of acts of nearness to God. There is agreement that charity and supplication reach [the deceased] with certainty, and everything besides these two falls within the disagreement — because for charity and supplication sound hadiths (ṣaḥīḥ) from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are established, and likewise for hajj and ʿumrah sound hadiths are established, whereas for everything other than all of that no explicit text (naṣṣ) has come from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the disagreement remains: is this among the fixed, quantified matters (al-muqaddarāt), into which analogical reasoning does not enter, or is it not among the fixed matters, so that analogy is possible in it? This is a point of disagreement in legal theory (uṣūl) that cannot be settled. Accordingly, those who perform the khatmah following upon the death of the deceased and wish to convey it to him — the more cautious and the better course for them is to give charity on his behalf and to supplicate for him, for that is what reaches him with no disagreement at all.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The sinking of the earth that will occur in the East, in the West and in the Arabian Peninsula

What is the sinking of the earth that will occur in the East, in the West and in the Arabian Peninsula?

The khasf is the earthquake that causes the face of the earth to go down beneath some of its own layers, and this is among the most severe kinds of earthquake. Many such sinkings have occurred in the easts and the wests of the earth, but it is not possible to assert with certainty that any one of these sinkings is the one meant in the hadith — even though three sinkings did come close together, one of them in the East, another in the West and another in the Arabian Peninsula. The one that occurred in the East is the sinking you have heard of in Iran; the sinking that occurred in the West is the sinking of the city of al-Asnam in Algeria; and the sinking in the Arabian Peninsula is the sinking of the city of Dhamar in Yemen. But it is not possible to assert with certainty that these are the ones meant in the hadith. Rather, these are all of them signs and admonitions, and God, exalted is He, says: {And We do not send the signs except to instil fear (59)} [Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:59]. They are a reminder to God's servants to believe in God, glorified and exalted, alone. But one does not assert with certainty that they are the ones meant by the hadith, because nothing has come that would indicate that specifically.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Taking the formulae of remembrance from one particular shaykh

On making it a condition that the formulae of remembrance (dhikr) be taken from one single, particular shaykh?

The remembrance of God is like the other matters of religion: it is taken from everyone who has narrated it and everyone who has transmitted it, and nowadays it is taken from books as well. So if a person turns to Sahih al-Bukhari, or Sahih Muslim, or the Muwatta', or to the books of the formulae of remembrance, and takes these formulae from them, that is sufficient. It has no special character over and above what holds for all the rulings.

flags.context: هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟
options: al-salkah — a complete recitation of the Qur'an dedicated to a deceased person
the 'threading' — a communal recitation in which the Qur'an is divided among those present and completed in one sitting
a Qur'an-completion gathering held for the dead
flags.note: Mauritanian/Shinqiti regional term, glossed by the questioner himself as the local name for the khatmah. Whether it denotes specifically the practice of dividing the text among a gathering so that it is completed at once (the sense the root س-ل-ك, 'to thread', suggests), or any dedicated completion, determines whether the term should be translated or kept in transliteration. The Sheikh's office should confirm the local practice before a fixed rendering is chosen. Comparable to the الكيص case in the style guide.

flags.arabic: هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه
flags.context: هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس أو ليس من المقدرات فيمكن القياس فيه هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه
options: This is a point of disagreement in legal theory that cannot be settled
This is a disagreement in legal theory that admits of no decisive resolution
This is a theoretical disagreement on which no ruling can be given
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh explicitly declines to settle this question. His closing advice — that charity and supplication are 'the more cautious and the better course' (al-aḥwaṭ ... wa-l-afḍal) — is a recommendation, NOT a ruling that the khatmah is forbidden or invalid. The English must not be presented or summarised in any way that converts it into a prohibition. Option 2 is rejected because it overstates: he declines to settle the uṣūl question, not to give any guidance at all.

flags.context: فالذين يفعلون الختمة عن دبر الميت ويريدون إيصالها إليه
options: following upon the death of the deceased
on behalf of the deceased after his death
at the conclusion of the rites for the deceased
flags.note: عن دبر idiomatically means 'immediately following'. Whether it points to the moment of death or to the end of the funeral rites is not determinable from the text, and the difference matters for describing the practice accurately.

flags.context: هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس
options: the matters whose measure is divinely fixed and so closed to analogy
flags.note: A technical uṣūl category not in the project glossary: rulings whose amounts or forms are set by revelation and therefore, on one view, not extendable by qiyās. It should be added to the glossary, since the whole argument of this fatwa turns on it.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

Four separate fatwas on one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as four separate items.
In the first item the heading and the question are identical in the Arabic and are printed one after the other. This duplication is in the source and has been kept.

Attribution of positions on the khatmah is load-bearing and has been kept exact: NOT reaching the deceased is attributed to Malik and al-Shafi'i; reaching him by analogy is attributed to Abu Hanifah and Ahmad; charity and supplication reaching him is reported as agreed by all. None of these is presented as the Sheikh's own position, and he states that the underlying question cannot be settled.

In the second and fourth items the question and the answer run together in a single paragraph with no marker in the Arabic. A paragraph break has been introduced in the English at the point where the answer begins; this is editorial.
Al-Asnam is the Algerian city now called Chlef, and Dhamar is in Yemen. The Sheikh names them without dates, and no dates or identifications of the earthquakes have been added.
مدينة الذمار in the source carries a definite article not normally written with the place name Dhamar; body_ar preserves the source.
